simple.meaning: נֶשֶׁךְ (neshek) is a Hebrew action word meaning “interest on a debt.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 12 times in Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Psalms, Proverbs, and 1 more, beginning at Exodus 22:24. The surrounding contexts include family, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נֶשֶׁךְ (H5392) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נֶשֶׁךְ (neshek) / H5392 is traced through Exodus 22:24, Leviticus 25:36, Leviticus 25:37, Deuteronomy 23:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5392. neshek נֶ֫שֶׁךְ noun [masculine] interest, usury (literally something bitten off ); — ׳נ absolute Exod 22:24 +; construct Deut 23:20 ; — with עַלֿ שִׂים Exod 22:24 (E); with מִן לָקַח Lev 25:36 , מִן הֵשִׁיב Ezek 18:17 , לָקַח 22:12 (no preposition), בְּנֶשֶׁךְ Lev 25:37 at interest , so Psa 15:5 ; Ezek 18:8 , 13 ; ׳בְּנ Prov 28:8 by usury ; as accusative of congnate meaning with verb Deut 23:20 (3 t. in verse).
